text:
sophia: Morning — quick sync: post-launch triage for release-v2. We have 4 high-severity bugs (two customer-facing), and a set of 6 enhancements requested by beta customers. Need to decide what goes into next sprint vs backlog. My proposal: 1) Fix customer-facing bugs blocker -> ship immediate patch 2) Defer lower-impact enhancements to next minor wave 3) Add one enhancement if it's low-cost and unlocks retention metric. Thoughts?

mike: Agree on prioritizing customer-facing bugs. Quick question: are any of the bugs regressions from the runtime change? I can do a quick root cause check today.

elaine: From CS: customer A reports generation truncation on long prompts -> high impact. Customer B has embed mismatch edge-case. Both want hotfix. I'm +1 for patch. Also, let's gate any enhancement that increases p99 latency >50ms.

mike: Took a look — truncation tied to KV cache sizing tweak. I can roll back a flag as fallback. Can we ship a canary config to 5% traffic? @ops-bot can we do that?

ops-bot: deploy-request received: canary 5% -> scheduled in 10m. Will post status.

sophia: OK scope: hotfix for those two bugs (clear rollback path), kill flag for KV sizing, add regression test in CI, telemetry dashboard to show prompt-length failure rate. Enhancements: pick one low-cost quickwin (UI prompt hint) for sprint. Others to backlog.

jordan: FYI impact on SLAs? If canary fails, ops runbook in incident channel ready. Also add customer comms template — I'll draft.

elaine: timeline? If ops canary is green, can we aim for patch by EOD? CS will prepare notes.

ops-bot: canary started -> 2/5 hosts healthy, monitoring metrics: latency +5ms, failures unchanged.

mike: Rolling flag rollback now. Patch build started: CI -> SUCCESS.

sophia: sweet. Thanks team. I'll update roadmap tracker and move the other enhancements to "next minor" with owner tags. :thumbsup:
